name: Grid trading bot

origin.authors: Retail exchange bots; formal analysis by Chen, Chen, Jang
origin.source_title: Dynamic Grid Trading Strategy: From Zero Expectation to Market Outperformance (arXiv 2506.11921)

how_it_works.simple: You place many buy orders below the price and sell orders above it, like rungs on a ladder. Every time the price bounces up and down between rungs, you make a small profit.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a shop that buys umbrellas cheap on sunny days and sells them dear on rainy days, as long as the weather keeps changing.
how_it_works.precise: Place geometric or arithmetic buy and sell limit orders at fixed intervals around a center price; each round trip earns the grid step minus fees. Chen et al. show that under simple random-walk assumptions the expected return of a static grid is essentially zero; profits from oscillation are offset by inventory losses when price leaves the range.

rule: Choose a range [L, U] and N levels with ratio step g; buy one unit each time price falls through a level and sell one unit each time it rises through the level above. The dynamic version resets the grid around the current price when price exits the range.
data_needed: 1-minute OHLC candles (Binance or OKX public API)
economic_rationale: Grids sell volatility: they profit when price mean-reverts inside a range. There is no clear risk premium; Chen et al. show the static grid has near-zero expectation before fees.
why_it_might_fail: When price trends out of the range the grid is left holding a falling asset or all cash in a rally. Fees eat small grids. The dynamic grid results come from a parameter sweep over one bull-heavy sample (2021-2024), so the best cells are in-sample picks.

reported_results.market: BTC and ETH, 1-minute data, OKX maker fee 0.08 percent
reported_results.notes: Read in the arXiv PDF. The dynamic grid IRR is reported as 'as high as 60-70%' for the best parameter cells, shown only in heatmaps; drawdown about 50 percent vs about 80 percent decline for buy-and-hold ETH. The static grid without fees fluctuates around zero, consistent with their zero-expectation result. No out-of-sample parameter selection.

implementations.notes: Code for the arXiv paper; no license file found via the GitHub API.
Has grid-style and pure market-making strategies.

relevance.reason: Popular with retail but has no expected edge; useful only as a negative control for parity.
